name: Kelp forest
notes: Cool rocky coasts with kelp canopies offshore: shoreline carries salt-spray cushions, rockweed and coastal scrub; underwater giant kelp, bull kelp and Laminaria form the forest with understory red/brown algae. Drawn on California/Pacific NW, Tasmania/NZ, Chile and North Atlantic (Norway, Scotland); underwater species flagged.

shrub.name: Heather
shrub.source: Calluna vulgaris, N Atlantic clifftop heath (Scotland, Norway), purple-flowered dwarf shrub 20-60 cm — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: Calluna vulgaris, N Atlantic clifftop heath (Scotland, Norway), purple-flowered dwarf shrub 20-60 cm — Wikipedia
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: low dense heather mound, purple haze in flower

growth.juvenile_note: Dust-fine seeds need light and sprout in 2-6 weeks on bare peat, sand or burnt ground. The seedling is a tiny green sprig of minute, overlapping, scale-like leaves in four rows; it branches into a small upright bush (pioneer phase), then a dense, rounded dome (building phase) that later spreads, thins and opens in the centre as it ages.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Calluna vulgaris (pioneer 0-6 yr, building 6-14, mature 14-25, degenerate after 25; lives about 30-40 yr on dry heaths; seeds rarely germinate without light; highly shade-intolerant); Gimingham 1960 Biological Flora of the British Isles.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (flowers Jul-Sep, mauve, in racemes; capsule); FEIS (flowers Jul-Nov in N America, wind and animal dispersal, seed bank long-lived); Gimingham 1960 (bees and wind pollinate; capsules ripen in autumn and shed seed over winter); counts approximate.

traits.native_range: Baccharis pilularis, California coastal bluffs above kelp coast, evergreen scrub 0

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny plumed achenes land on bare mineral soil and sprout in 2-4 weeks. The seedling has two small round cotyledons, then small, glossy, bright-green, wedge-shaped leaves with a few teeth, over a deep taproot. It branches quickly from the base into a dense, rounded or sprawling mound of stiff, crowded green twigs.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Baccharis pilularis (germination mostly within 15-30 d without pretreatment, shade-intolerant, poor seedling growth in shade, individuals live 10-15 yr but basal sprouting and layering extend it); first flowering age estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (dioecious, flowers Jul-Oct, 55 insect visitor species incl. honey bees, achenes 1-2 mm with 6-10 mm pappus, ripe Sep-Nov, dispersed Oct-Jan); counts are flower heads, estimated.

traits.native_range: Gaultheria shallon, Pacific NW headlands, evergreen shrub 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: dense glossy thicket, leaves held flat and layered

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seedlings on rotting logs and stumps (light needed to germinate): two small cotyledons, then leathery, finely toothed oval leaves. Very slow at first (only 8-13 cm after 2-3 years); then spreads by layering and rhizomes into a thicket of zigzag, reddish, glandular-hairy stems with glossy, thick, egg-shaped evergreen leaves.
growth.source: USDA FEIS species review (Gaultheria shallon): germination in 27-45 days, light required; seedlings slow, 3-5 in after 2-3 yr; flowers only at >=5 yr; twigs live 16+ yr and rhizomes for centuries; shade-tolerant but less vigorous under dense canopy.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (flowers May-Jul, white to pink urn-shaped flowers on terminal bracteate racemes, ~6 per twig, bee and fly pollinated; hairy blue-black pseudoberries 6-10 mm ripen Aug-Oct and may persist to December, ~126 seeds each; regular good crops). Fruit set, rot and crop estimated.

shrub.source: Suaeda taxifolia, S California coastal bluffs and salt marsh edge, grey-green fleshy shrub 0.5-1.5 m — Calflora

traits.native_range: Suaeda taxifolia, S California coastal bluffs and salt marsh edge, grey-green fleshy shrub 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two narrow, fleshy green cotyledons, then short, fleshy, finger-like leaves that are grey-green and often woolly. It branches low into a small succulent sprig and within a few years becomes a woody-based, mounded to sprawling grey-green subshrub on coastal bluffs, dunes and salt-marsh edges.
growth.source: Wikipedia Suaeda taxifolia (shrub or subshrub to ~1.5 m, woody below, fleshy hairy-waxy leaves; flowers 1-3 per cluster with leaf-like bracts, no petals, fleshy calyx; fruit a utricle in the calyx; salt marsh, beach, dune and scrub of S California and Baja). Germination, growth, flowering season and ages estimated from shrubby Suaeda.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia Suaeda taxifolia (petal-less flowers with fleshy hairy sepals, 1-3 per cluster; fruit a utricle enclosed by the calyx). Flowering months, wind/self pollination, ripening (one shiny dark seed ~1.5-2 mm) and crop estimated from Suaeda and other coastal chenopods.

ground.name: Torrey's surfgrass
ground.origin: Pacific coast, British Columbia to Baja

growth.juvenile_note: The crescent-shaped seed has two barbed arms that snag on branched coralline red algae on rock; the seedling roots into that turf and puts up a tuft of hair-fine green leaves. Rhizomes then creep over and bind to the rock, and the clump grows into a dense mop of wiry leaves up to 2 m long that streams in the surge.
growth.source: Flora of North America vol. 22 (Phyllospadix torreyi: leaves 0.5-1.5 mm wide, nearly round in section, to about 2 m; lower intertidal to subtidal on surf-swept rock, British Columbia to Baja California); seed attachment to coralline algae from surfgrass recruitment studies; ages estimated

repro.note: dioecious; pollen strands carried by water; barbed seeds catch on coralline algae

ground.source: Phyllospadix torreyi, Torrey's surfgrass, Pacific coast from British Columbia to Baja California, seagrass of surf-swept rock from the low intertidal into the shallow subtidal under the kelp, wiry leaves 0.5-1.5 mm wide to 2 m — Kew POWO / Flora of North America

bark.note: submerged; leaves sheathed on a creeping rhizome

ground.silhouette: submerged meadow of long green ribbons streaming with tide

growth.juvenile_note: The seed splits and a white seedling axis anchors in sandy mud; a green cotyledon is followed by 2-3 narrow, flat, bright green ribbon leaves from a sheath. The seedling soon grows a creeping white rhizome with roots at each node and new shoots along it, so a first-year plant is a short row of leafy tufts; leaf length (a few cm to over 1 m) depends on water depth and clarity.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Zostera marina): leaves to 1.2 cm wide and over 1 m long (a few cm in clear shallow water), perennial but may grow as an annual, several thousand seeds per m2, inflorescence about 10 cm, one meadow clone about 3000 years old. Germination, seedling growth, flowering age and shoot life estimated from eelgrass restoration studies.

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds are crescent-shaped with two barbed arms that snag on bushy coralline red algae; the seedling roots into the algal turf and puts up a small tuft of narrow, bright-green, thread-like leaves. Over years it forms rhizomes that bind to rock and makes dense emerald tufts of long, narrow (2-4 mm) ribbon leaves streaming in the surge.
growth.source: Wikipedia (seedlings establish among red coralline algae, attaching by small barbs and roots; rhizomes colonise rock in the mid to low intertidal); slow seedling establishment and ages estimated from surfgrass recruitment studies
